business_summary: Microsoft Corporation is a diversified US technology company spanning productivity software, Azure cloud infrastructure, and Windows and devices. It designs in-house Maia AI accelerators, builds and operates hyperscale Azure data centers, ships Copilot Studio and Agent 365 AI-application tooling, and is the anchor hyperscaler buyer whose capital spending drives data-center demand broadly. It sits on four links across two chains: ai-accelerators, hyperscale-datacenters and ai-applications on ai-infrastructure, and hyperscale-buildout-demand on data-center-moratoria.

exposure_summary.narrative: Microsoft's own FY2026 Q4 earnings materials state directly that quarterly capital expenditure reached $41 billion (up 70% year-over-year) and that companywide calendar-2026 capex guidance is approximately $175 billion, a first-party VERIFIED figure; but that guidance spans data centers, servers, offices, logistics and other property broadly, and is not broken into Maia-, Azure-AI-capacity- or Copilot-specific shares, nor into the three underlying ai-infrastructure link roles.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: No revenue-exposure percentage isolating AI-accelerator, hyperscale-datacenter or AI-application revenue is disclosed in sources on file: the $175 billion capex figure is a companywide capital-spending guide, not a segment revenue split, and no data/edgar/docs/MSFT.json filing is on disk this run to check for a finer breakdown.

crowdedness_caveats: Every one of Microsoft's four placements sits at CROWDED or OVER_CROWDED link heat; Microsoft is one of the largest and most heavily covered companies in public markets on every one of these AI angles simultaneously.
The $175 billion capex figure spans the whole company's property and equipment spending, not an AI-specific or per-link breakdown.

catalysts.claim: Microsoft's own fiscal 2026 Q4 earnings materials state capital expenditures of $41 billion for the quarter (up 70% year-over-year) and raise companywide calendar-2026 capex guidance to approximately $175 billion, first-party VERIFIED evidence the hyperscaler buildout is accelerating through the 2026 moratorium wave rather than pausing for it.

catalysts.claim: Microsoft states Agent 365 is generally available and works with prebuilt Microsoft 365 Copilot agents and agents built in Copilot Studio or Microsoft Foundry, a first-party disclosure of a shipping AI-applications product, not a roadmap promise.
Net debt to EBITDA of 0.05x, an FCF margin of 20.2% and a Piotroski F-score of 6 show Microsoft can fund a $175 billion capex program almost entirely from its own cash generation.

risks.claim: All four of Microsoft's placements sit in already-discovered links (ai-accelerators and hyperscale-buildout-demand both OVER_CROWDED; hyperscale-datacenters and ai-applications both CROWDED) with no money_corner anywhere; Microsoft is arguably the single most-covered name in the entire AI theme across every angle it touches.

The reverse-DCF solve implies a 35.6% five-year FCF CAGR at the current enterprise value (a 16.0-point spread versus the 10-year read), a high bar for a company already generating 331,839,000,000 in annual revenue to keep clearing while simultaneously funding $175 billion of annual capex.

None of Maia accelerator revenue, Azure AI-capacity revenue or Copilot/Agent 365 revenue is broken out separately from Microsoft's Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing segments, so the AI-specific exposure behind any single placement is unquantified.
